question:
Using the inverse-matrix method, solve the system
$$3x+2y=13$$
$$x-y=1$$

(a) Express the system in the form $AX=B$ and show that $A$ is invertible.

(b) Find $A^{-1}$ and hence determine $x$ and $y$.

(c) Verify the solution in both equations.

options.B:
(a) $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&2\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$, $|A|=-5$
(b) $A^{-1}=\frac15\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\1&-3\end{bmatrix}$ and $(x,y)=(2,3)$
(c) Only the second equation is satisfied
options.D:
(a) $|A|=0$, so $A$ is singular
(b) $A^{-1}$ does not exist
(c) The system has no solution
